description: Make permission-based fault-injection seams root-safe in the three test files that fail only because the suite runs as root (uid=0), where chmod-based fault injection is a no-op. All 25 current `npm test` failures (22 in c4b2a-mechanical-rollback-wiring, 2 in authorship-key-store-negative, 1 CCB-19 in mission-corridor-closure-binding) stem from this single OUTWARD/environmental root cause: root bypasses DAC, so a 0o000 file is still readable and a 0o500/0o400 target is still writable, so the injected fault never fires and the assertion fails. The code under test is CORRECT and must not change. The fix mirrors the canonical in-repo precedent in tests/first-encounter-admission.test.js: before each permission-dependent assertion, probe whether the running identity actually enforces the specific mode the test relies on; if it does not, call `t.skip("filesystem does not enforce modes for this process")` (or an equally honest, specific reason) and return, so the assertion is skipped honestly on root and still RUNS and PASSES on a mode-enforcing (non-root) environment such as CI ubuntu-latest. This change touches ONLY the three test files; it does NOT edit the G8 classifier allowlist (scripts/ci/classify-known-harness-failures.mjs) and does NOT weaken any gate — masking a real-looking assertion failure by name alone is explicitly forbidden by the project's no-false-GREEN hardening, so a skip is the only Ihsan-compliant path.
steps: Read tests/first-encounter-admission.test.js lines 190-285 to copy the exact `canEnforceModes` probe pattern and the honest skip-reason string `"filesystem does not enforce modes for this process"`. The probe does: chmod(path, 0o000) → try readdir/read → returns false (not enforced) if the read succeeds, true if it throws EACCES/EPERM → restores mode in finally.

Introduce a small, local, test-only probe helper in each of the three affected files (or a shared tiny helper imported by them) that detects whether the SPECIFIC permission denial the test depends on actually fires for the current process. For the directory-write seams (c4b2a: chmod 0500 on eventsDir), probe by chmod'ing a throwaway dir to 0o500 and attempting a write inside it, cleaning up after. For the directory/file-unreadable seams (c4b2a chmod 0000, authorship 0o000 read, CCB 0o400 write), probe the matching operation. The probe must be hermetic (its own tmp path) and must restore permissions in a finally block.

In tests/authorship-key-store-negative.test.js: wrap the two adversarial loader cases at ~lines 225-233 ("returns null for a zero-permission (unreadable) private key file") and ~lines 275-281 ("returns null for an unreadable public key file"). Convert each `it(name, async () => {...})` to `it(name, async (t) => {...})`, and immediately after creating the key but before `chmodSync(path, 0o000)`, probe enforcement; if not enforced, `t.skip("filesystem does not enforce modes for this process"); return;`. Keep the real assertion (`assert.equal(result, null)`) intact for enforcing environments.

In tests/c4b2a-mechanical-rollback-wiring.test.js: guard every test whose outcome depends on the chmod seam actually denying access. These are the 22 failing cases rooted at the seams on lines ~172 (`trip`), ~346 (apply hook), ~425 (chmod 0000 eventsDir), ~655, ~1443. For each affected top-level test, add a `t` parameter and, before relying on the seam producing a real failure/uncertainty, call the enforcement probe; if modes are not enforced, `t.skip("filesystem does not enforce modes for this process (root bypasses DAC; the permission-based fault-injection seam cannot fire)"); return;`. Where several tests share a `trip`/seam helper, it is acceptable to probe once per test at entry. Do not alter the assertions themselves or the production modules they exercise.

In tests/mission-corridor-closure-binding.test.js: guard the CCB-19 case at ~line 685-694 ("CCB-19: C2 resolves before corridor COMPLETE and a failed journal append recovers exactly") and the parent "corridor closure BINDING" test if the failure cascades to it. Add `t` to the signature, probe write-denial on a 0o400 file before `await chmod(journalPath, 0o400)`, and if the running identity can still write it, `t.skip("filesystem does not enforce modes for this process"); return;` so the `assert.match(interrupted, /EACCES|permission denied/i)` only runs where it is meaningful.

Run each of the three files in isolation with `node --test <file>` and confirm 0 failures: on this root sandbox the permission-dependent cases report as skipped (TAP `# skipped`), everything else still passes.

Run the full `npm test` and confirm the G8 classifier reports a clean run (exit 0) with `# fail 0` and zero `[G8 UNRECOGNIZED]` lines. The previously-failing 25 are now honest skips, so the classifier never sees an unrecognized `not ok`.

Add a concise honest note to docs/CURRENT_LIMITS.md recording the environmental constraint and the fix: that the permission-based fault-injection seams in these three suites are skipped (not faked) when the running identity does not enforce filesystem modes (e.g. root), that this leaves the corresponding adversarial invariants UNVERIFIED on such hosts (they are only VERIFIED on a mode-enforcing environment such as CI ubuntu-latest), and bind the note to HEAD SHA 01dbf8ffb7a9c251645967be1d4d08f16716e2f7. Do not overclaim: a skip proves the harness is honest, not that the adversarial property holds on root.

Emit a proof receipt as a plain JSON file under .agents/tasks/task-root-safe-fault-injection/ (e.g. receipt.json) recording: the HEAD SHA, the exact test commands run and their observed TAP summaries (before: 25 fail; after: 0 fail with N skipped), the three files changed, the classification (OUTWARD/environmental, root bypasses DAC), what the result proves (harness is now honest on non-mode-enforcing hosts; full suite is G8-clean) and what it does NOT prove (the adversarial permission invariants remain verified only on mode-enforcing environments; this does not run the governed Rust runtime, mint any value, or close Node0).

findings: ROOT CAUSE (empirically verified): suite runs as root (uid=0; `id` confirmed). Direct demonstration: `cat` of a 0o000 file succeeded (ROOT CAN READ 0000 FILE) and writing into a 0o500 dir succeeded (ROOT CAN WRITE INTO 0500 DIR). All 25 failures isolate to exactly 3 files (22+1+2=25, matching the full-suite `# fail 25`). CI runs on ubuntu-latest (non-root) where these pass. Canonical fix precedent exists at tests/first-encounter-admission.test.js (canEnforceModes + t.skip 'filesystem does not enforce modes for this process'). The G8 classifier (scripts/ci/classify-known-harness-failures.mjs) explicitly forbids name-only masking and requires an environmental CAUSE signature in the diagnostic block; root-induced assertion failures carry NO such signature, so allowlisting them would be a false-GREEN and is rejected — honest skips are the only compliant fix.
